rice_arsenic.decision: White basmati from California, boiled in plenty of water.
rice_arsenic.short_answer: Rice takes up more arsenic than other grains, and the bran holds most of it. Brown carries more than white; variety and origin matter more than color. White California basmati, rinsed and boiled in extra water, is the strong pick.
rice_arsenic.detail: Rice takes up more inorganic arsenic from soil and water than other grains, and the bran holds most of it. Healthy Babies Bright Futures measured brown rice at 129 ppb against 86 for white. By variety, basmati averaged 55 ppb and sushi rice 57, while plain long-grain and parboiled both averaged 101. Origin moves it as much as color does. Rice grown in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri and Texas tests highest, and California, India and Pakistan test lowest. Why the southern crop runs high is not settled. Those fields carry residue from decades of arsenical pesticides used on cotton, and the same fields also have sandier soil, which releases arsenic more readily than clay. Both explanations are published and neither has been shown to be the whole of it. Cooking is the other lever. Rinse the rice, boil it in a high ratio of water and pour the water off. The bran also carries phytic acid, so brown rice, when it is the choice, is bought organic and soaked overnight before cooking.
rice_arsenic.kristy_take: Take the white basmati from California. Rinse it, boil it in plenty of water and pour the water off.
buying_tips: Arsenic collects in the bran, so brown rice carries more than white.
Rinse it, boil it in plenty of water and pour the water off.

oats_steelcut_rolled_instant.decision: Plain organic oats, soaked overnight, then cooked.
oats_steelcut_rolled_instant.short_answer: Same grain, three ways: steel-cut is least processed, rolled is steamed and flattened, instant is pre-cooked and often pre-sweetened. Buy plain organic oats in any form. Soak them overnight with a little yogurt, whey or cider vinegar, then cook them.

Instant are pre-cooked and often come pre-sweetened, and the flavored packets are mostly added sugar. The traditional step is the soak. Oats go into warm water overnight with a spoonful of yogurt, whey or apple cider vinegar, which reduces their phytic acid, and get cooked in the morning. Many traditional cooks toasted the oats in butter or ghee first for flavor. Conventional oats may be sprayed with glyphosate shortly before harvest to dry the crop, and organic farming does not allow glyphosate.
oats_steelcut_rolled_instant.kristy_take: A bag of plain organic oats. Soak them the night before and cook them in the morning. Sweeten with fruit; the flavored packets are candy with an oat garnish.
buying_tips: Same grain in every form; the flavored packets are where the sugar is.

flour_basics.decision: Organic sprouted flour, or fresh-ground whole grain, soaked.
flour_basics.why: Whole grain flour keeps the bran and germ, and soaking or sprouting is how those were traditionally made digestible.
flour_basics.short_answer: Freshly ground organic whole grain flour, soaked before baking, is the top rung. Organic sprouted flour is next, with the soaking step done. Unbleached white is a limited use. Skip bleached white flour, and whole grain flour used without soaking.
flour_basics.detail: Refining strips the bran and germ and leaves the starchy endosperm, which is what makes white flour pale and shelf-stable. Whole grain flour keeps them, along with the phytic acid in the bran. Soaking the flour overnight with a little acid, or buying flour made from sprouted grain, is the traditional answer. The germ also carries oil, and milled flour stored for long periods, particularly in open bins, turns rancid. Fresh-ground from a small mill, bought in small amounts and kept cold, is the way around that. On white flour, the label must bear the word “Bleached” when a bleaching ingredient was used. Bromated flour has potassium bromate added. Enriched means B vitamins and iron were added back after refining took them out.
flour_basics.kristy_take: Fresh-ground or sprouted, organic, and soaked when it is not sprouted. Keep whole grain flour cold. The germ is still in it, and that oil turns.
buying_tips: Whole grain flour keeps the bran and germ; soak it, or buy it sprouted.

bulk_bins_buying.detail: Bulk strips out the packaging and the brand. Spices are the extreme case, where a scoop from a bin is usually fresher than a jar because the bin moves. The risk sits with the fatty items. Milled flour stored for long periods in open bins turns rancid, and nuts and seeds are best bought fresh in sealed packages rather than from bins. Rancidity announces itself: rancid nuts and seeds smell like old paint or crayons and taste sharp and bitter. Bring your own jars where the store allows it, and note the tare weight.
bulk_bins_buying.kristy_take: Bulk is unbeatable on beans and spices. Nuts, seeds and flour come in a sealed bag.

grains_beyond_rice.decision: Organic whole grains, soaked overnight before cooking.
grains_beyond_rice.why: Hulled grains keep their bran, and soaking is the traditional step that makes them digestible.
grains_beyond_rice.detail: Hulled barley is minimally processed to remove only the tough inedible outer hull. Pearl barley has been polished to remove some or all of the outer bran layer along with the hull. On barley and farro, “pearled” marks bran removed and “whole” or “hulled” marks bran kept. The bran carries phytic acid, so whole grains are soaked overnight in warm water with a little acid before cooking, or bought sprouted. Store-bought bulgur is parboiled and dried rather than soaked or sprouted, and quick-cooking grains skip the soak too. Variety is worth it on its own terms, since rotating grains means no single crop is the base of every meal. Buckwheat is not wheat at all. Millet and sorghum carry no gluten. The bitter coating on quinoa’s hull is called saponin.
grains_beyond_rice.kristy_take: Whole or hulled, organic, and soaked the night before. The bag says which grain kept its bran.
buying_tips: Pearled grains have some or all of the bran polished off; hulled loses only the hull.

breakfast_cereal.short_answer: Boxed cold cereal is extruded: a grain slurry forced through a small hole at high heat and pressure. Organic boxes are made the same way. Soaked, cooked porridge is the top rung; organic soaked granola is the boxed fallback.
breakfast_cereal.detail: Modern cold breakfast cereals are made by extrusion. The traditional breakfast grain is a porridge: whole grains soaked overnight and cooked, served with butter and cream. breakfast_cereal.kristy_take: A pot of soaked oats with butter and cream does the job the box claims to. If it has to be boxed, organic soaked granola.

raw_cider_vinegar.detail: Cider vinegar is made from apple juice by two fermentations. Yeast first turns the sugars into alcohol, making cider. Organic raw vinegar sits on the top rung of the traditional tiers, and distilled vinegar on the low one. Vinegar labeling rules set 4 grams of acetic acid per 100 mL. A diluted vinegar must say “diluted with water to __ percent acid strength”, never below 4 percent. A blend of spirit and cider vinegar is labeled as a blend, names in order of predominance. The mother is a cellulose film of acetic bacteria. It may remain in unfiltered vinegar, or be filtered out.
